shadow.$description: Layer 2. Elevation on a dark UI is carried by the surface step, not by shadow; these only add the last bit of separation that a stepped surface cannot give on its own, and in light theme they do most of the work because the surfaces there are all near-white. One soft shadow plus a hairline inset highlight is the whole budget. Values are pre-composed CSS strings rather than DTCG's structured shadow object, because that object has no way to express an inset and both of these need one.

raised.$description: A card or panel sitting on the base plane. The inset line is a single hairline of light along the top edge, the way a raised physical surface catches the light above it. Barely visible by design.

overlay.$description: A menu, popover or dialog floating over the whole page. The one place a shadow is allowed to be noticeable, because an overlay has to read as detached rather than merely lighter. Still soft and still tight: a large blur with a negative spread, not a heavy drop shadow.
